status: A0 narrow gate SURVIVES; broader joint fit required
question: Can a single boundary-aware entry mixture, learned only on training physical leaves and with no persistent paragraph state, reproduce the held-out Voynich entry-transition direction?

design.generator: body draws from a fixed manuscript token inventory; paragraph line0 alone is reweighted by a coarse entry/body token-shape score learned on training leaves
design.entry_shape: k/t presence x capped token length x first character x last character
design.heldout_direction: Voynich transition direction learned on training leaves only

decision: A boundary-aware nonsemantic generator can reproduce or exceed the scalar held-out entry-direction projection with one explicit short-lived entry-mixture mechanism. Therefore Phase60's entry signature alone does NOT reject hierarchical meaningless generation once paragraph-boundary awareness is granted.
critical_limitation: This is intentionally only the narrow preregistered gate. The generator was not yet required to jointly match Voynich near-family density, local-prev10 activation, line-position grammar, section modulation, token-frequency spectrum, or other Phase44-60 constraints. Its body generator in this optimized test is simplified and must not be treated as a successful whole-manuscript model.
interpretation: The explanatory cost of R60-A is now explicit: at minimum it needs a paragraph-boundary-conditioned token-form mixture. That mechanism is cheap enough to reproduce the entry direction, so the next discriminator must be joint constraint satisfaction and complexity, not entry existence by itself.
next: Phase61B: freeze a multi-target scorecard and test whether A0 can satisfy entry direction + near-family density/locality + line-position grammar simultaneously without adding new mechanisms. If it fails, any repair becomes A1 and pays an explicit complexity increment.
